text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A survey on the average net income per Dane since 1985 shows that Jutland, in west Denmark, has experienced greater economic growth than the rest of Denmark with the capital Copenhagen and environs below average.

--- The United Nations criticises Denmark in a human rights report for its slow handling of compensation for eskimo seal hunters forcibly evicted from Thule in northwestern Greenland in 1953 to make way for the building of a U.S. military base. Police dogs were used to keep protests down and some locals detained in prison for excessively long periods, the report alleges.

--- Imports of garbage from abroad (mainly Germany) are still on the increase as combustion and waste sites are relatively cheaper in Denmark, but often documentation does not state exactly what the refuse is and police are now investigating irregularities.

--- Danish cleaning group ISS is showing renewed interest in the Danish elderly care market with its Swedish unit ISS Care Service entering the local market as state authorities in Denmark consider privatising public sector elderly care.

--- The government's mishandling of British writer Salman Rusdie's visit to Denmark to receive a European literary prize is delaying agreement on the 1997 state budget. The leftist opposition Socialist People's Party says it will not continue negotiations before a parliamentary debate on the affair due Thursday. The minority government had hoped for a broad state budget deal already this week.
